description: Adversary emulation scripts for the MITRE ATT&CK Collection tactic (TA0009). Covers 10 scriptable parent techniques: data collection from the local filesystem (sensitive file type search), data collection from network shared drives (UNC recursive file listing), data staging (create staging directory and copy collected files), screen capture (.NET CopyFromScreen API), automated collection (batch file pattern matching pipeline), audio capture device enumeration, video/camera device enumeration, archive collected data (Compress-Archive to ZIP), email collection (MAPI profile and PST file enumeration), and clipboard data capture (Windows Clipboard API). All scripts are read-only or use only the Defender-excluded temp directory. Automatic cleanup for all artefacts.
author: X3M.AI
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2019/2022 test machine with Morgana agent installed
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) onboarded and data connector active in Microsoft Sentinel
No Administrator privileges required for any script in this pack
For T1113 (screen capture): a display session is required (does not work on headless Server Core without desktop session)
For T1039 (network share data): at least one accessible UNC share is beneficial but not required - the enumeration attempt generates telemetry regardless
For T1114 (email collection): Microsoft Outlook must be installed or an Outlook PST file must exist in the default profile path. Script enumerates without reading email content.
Test environment only - never run against production systems or monitored production environments

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1005-Data from Local System
scripts.description: Searches the local filesystem for sensitive file types commonly targeted by adversaries for data collection: documents (*.docx, *.xlsx, *.pdf), plaintext data (*.txt, *.csv), credential stores (*.kdbx, *.pfx, *.pem, *.key), and remote access files (*.rdp). Reports the count and metadata of matches without reading file content. Also enumerates high-value directories (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, AppData/Roaming). The file system traversal pattern across sensitive extensions is a MDE collection behavioral indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1005 - Data from Local System (sensitive file type collection recon)'; $searchRoot = '#{excalibur_col_t1005_search_path}'; $sensitiveExt = @('*.docx','*.xlsx','*.pdf','*.txt','*.csv','*.kdbx','*.pfx','*.pem','*.key','*.rdp','*.ps1','*.bat','*.config','*.json'); Write-Host ('[INFO] Search root: ' + $searchRoot + ' | Extensions: ' + ($sensitiveExt -join ', ')); try { $allFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $searchRoot -Recurse -Include $sensitiveExt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -Force; Write-Host ('[INFO] Total sensitive files found: ' + $allFiles.Count); $grouped = $allFiles | Group-Object Extension | Sort-Object Count -Descending; foreach ($g in $grouped) { Write-Host ('    ' + $g.Name + ': ' + $g.Count + ' file(s)') }; if ($allFiles.Count -gt 0) { Write-Host '[INFO] Top 5 most recently modified:'; $allFiles | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.FullName + ' | ' + [math]::Round($_.Length/1KB,1) + ' KB | ' + $_.LastWriteTime.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')) } } } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] File search error: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] High-value directory enumeration:'; $hvDirs = @( [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:USERPROFILE, 'Desktop'), [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:USERPROFILE, 'Documents'), [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:USERPROFILE, 'Downloads'), [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:APPDATA, 'Microsoft', 'Windows', 'Recent'), 'C:\Users\Public\Documents' ); foreach ($dir in $hvDirs) { if (Test-Path $dir) { $count = @(Get-ChildItem $dir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Count; Write-Host ('    ' + $dir + ': ' + $count + ' item(s)') } else { Write-Host ('    ' + $dir + ': not found') } }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1005 - Local data collection recon completed. Sentinel target: Sensitive file type search across user directories (MDE behavioral - bulk file extension search pattern)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1005 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only file enumeration'
scripts.detection_rule: Sensitive file type search across user directories (bulk file extension search pattern)

scripts.id: Excalibur - Collection-T1039-Data from Network Shared Drive
scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1039-Data from Network Shared Drive
scripts.description: Enumerates files on a network share via UNC path, simulating adversary collection of data from shared drives. Lists files by extension, identifies high-value targets (documents, credentials, configs), and reports total size. No file content is read. Also enumerates mapped network drives via Get-SmbMapping and Get-PSDrive. The UNC path traversal generates SMB outbound network telemetry in MDE regardless of share accessibility.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1039 - Data from Network Shared Drive (UNC share file enumeration)'; $uncPath = '#{excalibur_col_t1039_unc_path}'; Write-Host ('[INFO] Target UNC: ' + $uncPath); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/3: UNC share file enumeration'; try { $shareFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $uncPath -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -Force -Depth 3; Write-Host ('[INFO] Files found on share: ' + $shareFiles.Count); $sensitiveOnShare = $shareFiles | Where-Object { $_.Extension -imatch '\.(docx|xlsx|pdf|txt|csv|kdbx|pfx|pem|key|rdp|ps1|bat|config|json|xml)$' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Sensitive file types on share: ' + $sensitiveOnShare.Count); $sensitiveOnShare | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.FullName + ' | ' + [math]::Round($_.Length/1KB,1) + ' KB') }; $totalSize = ($shareFiles | Measure-Object Length -Sum -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Sum; Write-Host ('[INFO] Total share data size: ' + [math]::Round($totalSize/1MB,2) + ' MB') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] UNC enumeration result: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (expected if share not accessible - SMB connection attempt was generated as network telemetry)') }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/3: Mapped network drives (Get-SmbMapping)'; try { $mapped = Get-SmbMapping -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($mapped) { $mapped | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.LocalPath + ' -> ' + $_.RemotePath) } } else { Write-Host '    No mapped drives found' } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/3: All PSDrive network paths'; $netDrives = Get-PSDrive -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayRoot -match '\\\\' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Network PSDrives: ' + $netDrives.Count); Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1039 - Network share data collection recon completed. Sentinel target: Bulk file enumeration via UNC path (MDE - SMB outbound + recursive file listing on network share)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1039 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only UNC enumeration'
scripts.detection_rule: Bulk file enumeration via UNC path (SMB outbound + recursive file listing on network share)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1074-Data Staged
scripts.description: Creates a staging directory in the Defender-excluded temp path and populates it with copies of several local files (hosts, Windows version info, environment dump) to simulate adversary data staging prior to exfiltration. Reports staging directory size and file count. All staged files are deleted after the test. The creation of a staging directory and bulk file copy to a non-standard path is a MDE collection behavioral detection indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1074 - Data Staged (create staging directory and stage collected files)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}'; $stagingName = '#{excalibur_col_t1074_staging_dir}'; $stagingPath = Join-Path $tmpDir $stagingName; try { if (Test-Path $stagingPath) { Remove-Item $stagingPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stagingPath -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Write-Host ('[INFO] Staging directory created: ' + $stagingPath); $filesToStage = @( @{ Src='C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts'; Name='MorganaTest-hosts.txt' }, @{ Src=(Join-Path $env:WINDIR 'System32\license.rtf'); Name='MorganaTest-wininfo.rtf' } ); $staged = 0; foreach ($f in $filesToStage) { if (Test-Path $f.Src) { $dest = Join-Path $stagingPath $f.Name; Copy-Item -Path $f.Src -Destination $dest -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if (Test-Path $dest) { Write-Host ('    Staged: ' + $f.Name + ' (' + (Get-Item $dest).Length + ' bytes)'); $staged++ } } }; $env:COMPUTERNAME + ' - ' + $env:USERNAME + ' - ' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') | Set-Content (Join-Path $stagingPath 'MorganaTest-sysinfo.txt') -Encoding UTF8; $staged++; Write-Host ('    Staged: MorganaTest-sysinfo.txt'); Get-ChildItem $env:USERPROFILE -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -imatch '\.(docx|xlsx|pdf|txt)$' } | Select-Object -First 3 | ForEach-Object { Copy-Item $_.FullName (Join-Path $stagingPath ('MorganaTest-' + $_.Name)) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $staged++; Write-Host ('    Staged: ' + $_.Name) }; $totalItems = @(Get-ChildItem $stagingPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Count; $totalSize = (Get-ChildItem $stagingPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum; Write-Host ('[INFO] Staging summary: ' + $totalItems + ' files | ' + [math]::Round($totalSize/1KB,1) + ' KB total'); Start-Sleep 2; Remove-Item $stagingPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1074 - Data staging completed and cleaned up. Sentinel target: Files copied to staging directory in non-standard path (MDE behavioral - bulk file copy to ProgramData staging location)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $stagingPath -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}' '#{excalibur_col_t1074_staging_dir}') -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1074 cleanup: staging directory removed'
scripts.detection_rule: Files copied to staging directory in non-standard path (bulk file copy to ProgramData)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1113-Screen Capture
scripts.description: Captures the primary screen using the .NET System.Drawing.Graphics.CopyFromScreen API and saves it to a PNG file in the Defender-excluded temp directory, then deletes it immediately. Screen capture is widely used by adversaries for situational awareness, credential harvesting from visible windows, and data collection. The use of System.Drawing CopyFromScreen from a non-UI process and the PNG file creation are MDE behavioral collection indicators. Requires a display session (not headless Server Core).
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1113 - Screen Capture (.NET CopyFromScreen API)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $screenshotPath = Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1113-screenshot.png'; try { Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms -ErrorAction Stop; Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing -ErrorAction Stop; $screen = [System.Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VirtualScreen; $width = $screen.Width; $height = $screen.Height; $x = $screen.Left; $y = $screen.Top; Write-Host ('[INFO] Virtual screen: ' + $width + 'x' + $height + ' at (' + $x + ',' + $y + ')'); $bitmap = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap($width, $height, [System.Drawing.Imaging.PixelFormat]::Format32bppArgb); $graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bitmap); $graphics.CopyFromScreen($x, $y, 0, 0, (New-Object System.Drawing.Size($width, $height)), [System.Drawing.CopyPixelOperation]::SourceCopy); $graphics.Dispose(); $bitmap.Save($screenshotPath, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png); $bitmap.Dispose(); $fileInfo = Get-Item $screenshotPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($fileInfo) { Write-Host ('[INFO] Screenshot captured: ' + $screenshotPath + ' | Size: ' + [math]::Round($fileInfo.Length/1KB,1) + ' KB | Resolution: ' + $width + 'x' + $height) } else { Write-Host '[WARN] Screenshot file not found after save - may be running headless (Server Core without display)' }; Remove-Item $screenshotPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1113 - Screen capture completed and removed. Sentinel target: Screen capture via System.Drawing CopyFromScreen API (MDE behavioral - screenshot API usage from non-UI process)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message + ' - if running headless, screen capture is not available'); Remove-Item $screenshotPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}' 'MorganaTest-T1113-screenshot.png') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1113 cleanup: screenshot file removed'
scripts.detection_rule: Screen capture via System.Drawing CopyFromScreen API (MDE behavioral collection)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1119-Automated Collection
scripts.description: Executes an automated collection pipeline using a PowerShell one-liner that combines Get-ChildItem recursive search with Where-Object filtering and Export-Csv output, simulating an adversary automated collection script. The pipeline searches for sensitive files across user profile directories, collects metadata (path, size, date, extension), and writes a CSV inventory to the Defender-excluded temp directory. The CSV is deleted after creation. Automated bulk file enumeration and metadata export to CSV are well-known collection automation patterns.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1119 - Automated Collection (pipeline: file search + filter + CSV export)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $csvPath = Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1119-collection-inventory.csv'; try { Write-Host '[INFO] Running automated collection pipeline: GCI -Recurse | Where Extension | Select metadata | Export-Csv'; $sensitiveExts = @('.docx','.xlsx','.pdf','.txt','.csv','.kdbx','.pfx','.pem','.key','.rdp','.ps1','.config','.json','.xml'); $collected = Get-ChildItem -Path $env:USERPROFILE -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -Force | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in $sensitiveExts } | Select-Object FullName, Extension, Length, LastWriteTime, @{N='SizeKB';E={[math]::Round($_.Length/1KB,2)}}; $collectedArr = @($collected); Write-Host ('[INFO] Files matching sensitive extensions in ' + $env:USERPROFILE + ': ' + $collectedArr.Count); if ($collectedArr.Count -gt 0) { $collectedArr | Export-Csv -Path $csvPath -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction Stop; $csvInfo = Get-Item $csvPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Collection inventory CSV written: ' + $csvPath + ' | ' + $csvInfo.Length + ' bytes | ' + $collectedArr.Count + ' records'); $collectedArr | Select-Object -First 3 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.FullName + ' | ' + $_.SizeKB + ' KB') } } else { 'MorganaTest-T1119-NoFilesFound' | Set-Content $csvPath -Encoding UTF8; Write-Host '[INFO] No matching files found in user profile - placeholder CSV written (expected in clean test environment)' }; Remove-Item $csvPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1119 - Automated collection pipeline completed. Sentinel target: Automated file collection and inventory export to CSV (MDE behavioral - bulk GCI pipeline + Export-Csv to temp path)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $csvPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}' 'MorganaTest-T1119-collection-inventory.csv') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1119 cleanup: CSV inventory file removed'
scripts.detection_rule: Automated file collection and inventory export to CSV (bulk GCI pipeline + Export-Csv)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1123-Audio Capture
scripts.description: Enumerates audio input devices (microphones) via three methods: WMI Win32_SoundDevice, .NET System.Speech SpeechRecognitionEngine (if available), and the Windows Multimedia API DirectShow device enumeration via COM. No audio is recorded - the enumeration of audio capture devices from a non-audio application is the MDE behavioral collection indicator. Adversaries enumerate audio devices prior to setting up audio capture for surveillance.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1123 - Audio Capture (audio input device enumeration)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 1/3: WMI Win32_SoundDevice enumeration'; try { $soundDevices = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_SoundDevice -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Sound devices (WMI): ' + $soundDevices.Count); $soundDevices | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Name + ' | Status: ' + $_.Status + ' | Manufacturer: ' + $_.Manufacturer) } } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] WMI Win32_SoundDevice: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 2/3: Registry audio device enumeration'; try { $audioRegPath = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\MMDevices\Audio\Capture'; if (Test-Path $audioRegPath) { $captureDevices = Get-ChildItem $audioRegPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Audio capture devices in registry: ' + $captureDevices.Count); $captureDevices | Select-Object -First 3 | ForEach-Object { $props = Get-ItemProperty (Join-Path $_.PSPath 'Properties') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('    DeviceId: ' + $_.PSChildName) } } else { Write-Host '[INFO] Audio capture registry path not found (no audio input devices registered)' } } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] Audio registry: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 3/3: DirectShow audio capture filter enumeration via COM'; try { $dmoCatId = '{33D9A762-90C8-11D0-BD43-00A0C911CE86}'; $devEnum = New-Object -ComObject 'DirectShow.DeviceEnum' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($devEnum) { Write-Host '[INFO] DirectShow DeviceEnum COM instantiated (audio capture category query)'; [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ReleaseComObject($devEnum) | Out-Null } else { Write-Host '[INFO] DirectShow DeviceEnum COM not available (expected in some environments)' } } catch { Write-Host '[INFO] DirectShow COM: not available in this environment' }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1123 - Audio capture device enumeration completed. Sentinel target: Audio input device enumeration from non-audio process (MDE behavioral - WMI Win32_SoundDevice + registry audio device access)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1123 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only device enumeration'
scripts.detection_rule: Audio input device enumeration from non-audio process (WMI Win32_SoundDevice + registry access)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1125-Video Capture
scripts.description: Enumerates video capture devices (webcams, screen capture devices) via WMI Win32_PnPEntity (camera PnP class), the Windows registry (imaging device class GUID), and MediaFoundation device source enumeration via COM. No video is recorded or streamed. Adversaries enumerate video devices prior to setting up video/webcam capture for surveillance. The cross-method device enumeration from a non-video application is the MDE behavioral collection indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1125 - Video Capture (video/camera device enumeration)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 1/3: WMI Win32_PnPEntity camera class enumeration'; try { $cameras = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_PnPEntity -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PNPClass -imatch 'Camera|Image|Video' -or $_.Name -imatch 'Camera|Webcam|Video' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Camera/video PnP devices found: ' + @($cameras).Count); $cameras | Select-Object -First 3 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Name + ' | Class: ' + $_.PNPClass + ' | Status: ' + $_.Status) } } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] WMI camera enum: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 2/3: Registry imaging/camera device class enumeration'; $cameraClassGuids = @('{6bdd1fc6-810f-11d0-bec7-08002be2092f}', '{ca3e7ab9-b4c3-4ae6-8251-579ef933890f}'); foreach ($guid in $cameraClassGuids) { $regPath = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Class\' + $guid; if (Test-Path $regPath) { $devices = Get-ChildItem $regPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PSChildName -match '^\d' }; Write-Host ('[INFO]   Registry class ' + $guid + ': ' + $devices.Count + ' device(s)'); $devices | Select-Object -First 2 | ForEach-Object { $driverDesc = (Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath -Name 'DriverDesc' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)?.DriverDesc; Write-Host ('    ' + $_.PSChildName + ' -> ' + $driverDesc) } } else { Write-Host ('[INFO]   Registry class ' + $guid + ': not found') } }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 3/3: Windows MediaFoundation video source enumeration (MFEnumDeviceSources pattern)'; try { $mfRegPath = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Media Foundation'; if (Test-Path $mfRegPath) { Write-Host ('[INFO]   MediaFoundation registry entries: ' + @(Get-ChildItem $mfRegPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Count) } } catch {}; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1125 - Video capture device enumeration completed. Sentinel target: Camera/video device enumeration from non-video process (MDE behavioral - PnP device class query + imaging registry access)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1125 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only device enumeration'
scripts.detection_rule: Camera/video device enumeration from non-video process (WMI PnP + imaging registry access)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1560-Archive Collected Data
scripts.description: Creates a ZIP archive of a small set of test files using PowerShell Compress-Archive, simulating adversary compression of collected data prior to exfiltration. Also demonstrates the alternative compress-lz4 pattern via .NET GZipStream (in-memory). The archive is created in the Defender-excluded temp directory and immediately deleted. Compress-Archive creating a ZIP in a non-standard location is a well-known collection pre-exfiltration pattern monitored by MDE.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1560 - Archive Collected Data (Compress-Archive ZIP + GZipStream pattern)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $archiveName = '#{excalibur_col_t1560_archive_name}'; $archivePath = Join-Path $tmpDir $archiveName; $sourceDir = Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1560-sources'; try { if (Test-Path $sourceDir) { Remove-Item $sourceDir -Recurse -Force }; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $sourceDir -Force | Out-Null; 'MorganaTest data file 1 - simulated collected document' | Set-Content (Join-Path $sourceDir 'doc1.txt') -Encoding UTF8; 'MorganaTest data file 2 - simulated collected spreadsheet' | Set-Content (Join-Path $sourceDir 'data2.csv') -Encoding UTF8; 'MorganaTest-hostname=' + $env:COMPUTERNAME | Set-Content (Join-Path $sourceDir 'sysinfo.txt') -Encoding UTF8; Write-Host ('[INFO] Source files created in: ' + $sourceDir); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/2: Compress-Archive to ZIP (primary collection archiving pattern)'; Compress-Archive -Path $sourceDir -DestinationPath $archivePath -CompressionLevel Optimal -Force -ErrorAction Stop; $archiveInfo = Get-Item $archivePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] ZIP archive created: ' + $archivePath + ' | Size: ' + $archiveInfo.Length + ' bytes'); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/2: In-memory GZipStream compression (alternative archiving technique - no file creation)'; try { $testData = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes('MorganaTest-T1560-GZipCompressedData'); $ms = New-Object System.IO.MemoryStream; $gz = New-Object System.IO.Compression.GZipStream($ms, [System.IO.Compression.CompressionMode]::Compress); $gz.Write($testData, 0, $testData.Length); $gz.Close(); Write-Host ('[INFO] GZipStream in-memory: input=' + $testData.Length + ' bytes -> compressed=' + $ms.Length + ' bytes (ratio=' + [math]::Round($ms.Length/$testData.Length*100,1) + '%)'); $ms.Dispose() } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] GZipStream: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Remove-Item $archivePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item $sourceDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1560 - Data archiving completed and cleaned up. Sentinel target: Compress-Archive creating ZIP in non-standard temp path (MDE behavioral - archive creation pre-exfiltration pattern)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $archivePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item $sourceDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_col_temp_dir}'; Remove-Item (Join-Path $tmpDir '#{excalibur_col_t1560_archive_name}') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item (Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1560-sources') -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1560 cleanup: archive and source dir removed'
scripts.detection_rule: Compress-Archive creating ZIP in non-standard temp path (archive creation pre-exfiltration pattern)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1114-Email Collection
scripts.description: Enumerates Outlook MAPI profile configuration from the registry and searches for Outlook PST/OST data files on the local filesystem, simulating adversary reconnaissance of email data stores prior to email collection. No email content is read or copied. Also checks for mail-related registry keys (accounts, autodiscover). Adversaries target Outlook data files to collect sensitive email communications. The pattern of MAPI registry access combined with PST file path enumeration is monitored by MDE.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1114 - Email Collection (MAPI profile + PST/OST file enumeration)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: Outlook MAPI profile registry enumeration'; $mapiProfilePath = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows Messaging Subsystem\Profiles'; try { if (Test-Path $mapiProfilePath) { $profiles = Get-ChildItem $mapiProfilePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] MAPI profiles found: ' + $profiles.Count); $profiles | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    Profile: ' + $_.PSChildName) } } else { Write-Host '[INFO] No MAPI profiles found in registry (Outlook not configured)' } } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] MAPI profile registry: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: PST/OST data file search'; $pstSearchPaths = @( [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:LOCALAPPDATA, 'Microsoft', 'Outlook'), [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:USERPROFILE, 'Documents', 'Outlook Files'), [System.IO.Path]::Combine($env:USERPROFILE, 'AppData', 'Local', 'Microsoft', 'Outlook') ); $pstFound = 0; foreach ($path in $pstSearchPaths) { if (Test-Path $path) { $pstFiles = Get-ChildItem $path -Recurse -Include *.pst,*.ost -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $pstFound += $pstFiles.Count; Write-Host ('[INFO]   ' + $path + ': ' + $pstFiles.Count + ' PST/OST file(s)'); $pstFiles | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.FullName + ' | ' + [math]::Round($_.Length/1MB,2) + ' MB') } } else { Write-Host ('[INFO]   Not found: ' + $path) } }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Total PST/OST files found: ' + $pstFound); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: Outlook account registry (email addresses configured)'; $outlookAcctPath = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Profiles'; try { if (Test-Path $outlookAcctPath) { $acctProfiles = Get-ChildItem $outlookAcctPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Outlook 16 profiles: ' + $acctProfiles.Count); $acctProfiles | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.PSChildName) } } else { Write-Host '[INFO] Outlook 16 profile registry not found' } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: Autodiscover registry (Exchange server discovery)'; $adPath = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\AutoDiscover'; if (Test-Path $adPath) { $adProps = Get-ItemProperty $adPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Autodiscover settings found: ' + ($adProps.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch '^PS' } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name) -join ', ') } else { Write-Host '[INFO] No Autodiscover registry settings found' }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1114 - Email collection reconnaissance completed. Sentinel target: MAPI profile and PST data file access (MDE behavioral - Outlook registry + PST file enumeration pattern)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1114 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only registry and file enumeration'
scripts.detection_rule: MAPI profile and PST data file enumeration (Outlook registry + PST file access pattern)

scripts.name: Excalibur - Collection-T1115-Clipboard Data
scripts.description: Reads the current Windows clipboard contents using the .NET System.Windows.Forms Clipboard API, simulating adversary collection of clipboard data (passwords typed then pasted, copied sensitive information, authentication tokens). Also writes a test value to the clipboard and reads it back to demonstrate the full write/read cycle used by clipboard injection techniques. Clipboard content is logged only as metadata (type and size), not as actual values. The Clipboard.GetData API call from a non-UI process is a MDE behavioral collection indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1115 - Clipboard Data (Windows Clipboard API access)'; try { Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/3: Read current clipboard contents (type and size only - value not logged)'; $currentText = $null; $currentData = $null; try { $currentText = [System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetText(); if ($currentText) { Write-Host ('[INFO] Clipboard TEXT: ' + $currentText.Length + ' chars, ' + @($currentText.Split([char]10)).Count + ' line(s) (content not shown)') } else { Write-Host '[INFO] Clipboard TEXT: empty' } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] GetText: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; try { $dataObj = [System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetDataObject(); if ($dataObj) { $formats = $dataObj.GetFormats(); Write-Host ('[INFO] Clipboard formats present: ' + ($formats -join ', ')) } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] GetDataObject: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/3: Write test value to clipboard (clipboard injection simulation)'; try { [System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::SetText('MorganaTest-T1115-ClipboardCapture-' + (Get-Date -Format 'HHmmss')); Write-Host '[INFO] Test value written to clipboard (SetText API call)' } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] SetText: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/3: Read back injected value (confirm clipboard access)'; try { $readBack = [System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetText(); if ($readBack -match 'MorganaTest-T1115') { Write-Host ('[INFO] Clipboard read-back: MorganaTest value confirmed (' + $readBack.Length + ' chars)') } else { Write-Host '[INFO] Clipboard read-back: value not found (another process may have cleared it)' }; [System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::Clear() } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] Read-back: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1115 - Clipboard data access completed. Sentinel target: Clipboard API access from non-UI process (MDE behavioral - System.Windows.Forms Clipboard.GetText from PowerShell)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message) }
scripts.cleanup_command: try { Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; [System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::Clear() } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] T1115 cleanup: clipboard cleared'
scripts.detection_rule: Clipboard API access from non-UI process (Clipboard.GetText from PowerShell)
